runs.detail: The planner is not hallucinating - it is right, and the format fact is the weak link. The capability it insisted on cites public_symbol:aspose.note.saveformat, and the fact set carries five SUPPORTED public symbols evidencing PDF export: aspose.note.SaveFormat (enum), aspose.note.model.PdfSaveOptions (class), aspose.note.saving.pdf_writer (module), aspose.note.saving.pdf_writer.write_pdf (function) and aspose.note.Document.Save (method). plan_checks (planning.py:525) builds its verdict from facts.by_kind('format') alone, so 'no fact verifies that format' is true only of format-kind facts. format:output.pdf carries exactly four evidence lines and every one is a failure: README.md line 119 (example 2) and line 235 (example 10), each paired with 'examples.json | example N: FAILED; RuntimeError'. formats.py has two routes to SUPPORTED and both are shut. THE EXECUTED ROUTE: examples 2 and 10 are the only two that write a .pdf and both failed identically - 'File .../aspose/note/saving/pdf_writer.py, line 1745, in write_pdf / from reportlab.lib.utils import ImageReader / ModuleNotFoundError: No module named reportlab'. reportlab>=3.6 is a DECLARED dependency of this repository, pyproject.toml lines 29-30, [project.optional-dependencies] pdf = ["reportlab>=3.6"]. All 12 examples record build_verified true, so the real wheel installed and the source fallback never ran; the wheel was installed without extras, and _declared_dependencies (python_examples.py:322-333) reads project.dependencies only - project.optional-dependencies is read by neither path, and Note's base dependencies list is literally []. THE STATIC-CORROBORATION ROUTE: ran format_declarations(root, 46 py files) directly against the pinned clone and it returns 0. python_format_declarations.py is shaped for one architecture - _declarations skips every file not literally named FileFormat.py (line 128) and _registrations needs a register_plugin(...) call (line 162). Note has neither: find -name FileFormat.py is empty and grep -rn register_plugin is empty. Yet both of section 22.1's independent static sources are plainly in its source - the declaration at src/aspose/note/enums.py:6-7 (class SaveFormat(Enum): Pdf = 'pdf') and a 1,828-line, emphatically non-stub exporter at src/aspose/note/saving/pdf_writer.py.

proposals.defect: An identifier spelled verbatim inside a SUPPORTED fact is refused unless that fact is kind example or the spelling sits in a shell-command fence, so a scope_limitations unit cannot name the member it is about. Arrival item 44 fixed the sibling half (the command fence) and command_block_tokens' own docstring records that the scoping was deliberate: 'Tokens of a fact's running prose, of a code span, and of a source-language fence stay out: an upstream README that merely mentions a symbol the surface no longer carries must not thereby license prose to spell it in a code span.' That reasoning is sound for a capability claim and lane E does not propose reversing it. What it does not cover is a limitation, whose whole content is that the member is NOT implemented and whose only honest source is the repository's own limitations list.
discriminators_the_measurement_supports: (a) scope by citation - a token spelled verbatim inside a SUPPORTED fact THIS UNIT CITES is spellable, which is stricter than item 44's fence rule since the fence rule needs no citation at all

(b) scope by section - scope_limitations units may spell a member of an already allowed symbol when the exact spelling appears in a cited SUPPORTED fact, since a negative claim cannot mis-advertise a surface
proposals.caution: allowed_identifiers feeds unit_checks, renderer.prose and BC-04 from one set, so fixing the guard alone would only move the rejection to BC-04 - its own docstring says so. Lane E explicitly does NOT propose 'admit every token of every SUPPORTED fact', which is the risk item 44 named.
proposals.family: Third measurement in one family: item 44 (a token inside an inherited command fence refused at authoring) and arrival item 68, admitted hours ago in 0fecf88 (repair/targeted.py::repair_packet strips inherited_unit entirely, so repair has nothing citable), are the same mis-handling of inherited_unit - the fact kind carrying the repository's own README text - at two other sites. E9 is the authoring-time, inline-code-span site.

proposals.defect: (1) The example runner installs the package but never the extras its manifest declares, on either path: the wheel path requests no extras and _declared_dependencies reads project.dependencies only. Note's PDF writer needs reportlab, a declared optional dependency, so both of its .pdf examples failed and the only executable route to format:output.pdf SUPPORTED closed. (2) The Python format-declaration extractor can only see the Aspose.3D plugin architecture (a file literally named FileFormat.py, a register_plugin call), so for every Python repository not built that way a format is reachable only through an executed example - 0 declarations found for Note despite SaveFormat.Pdf and a 1,828-line non-stub pdf_writer.
proposals.lane_e_recommends: (1) first, and in its narrow form: an example that FAILS with 'ModuleNotFoundError: No module named X' is retried once with the declared extra that provides X - the same fold-not-reject retry verify_python_examples already runs for NEEDS_INPUT, and the shape the G3 second pass's own Font predicate proposes. Installing every extra is not proposed: this manifest's others are test-pdf and dev, which no example needs. Nothing is weakened - if examples 2 and 10 execute, format:output.pdf becomes SUPPORTED by the executed route and the title check passes on its own terms.
proposals.not_proposed: No change to plan_checks, and no relaxation of section 22.1's two-independent-source rule - Note satisfies that rule on its own source; the extractor cannot see it.
proposals.content_nuance_for_whoever_reruns: PDF export here is behind an optional extra, so the honest capability title may need to say so, and the extra is itself a fact the candidate should carry.
